extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the proper conduct when facing disaster and losing one's kingdom.
Bhishma advises that the best course when losing family, happiness, and wealth is to remain steadfast, as this preserves health and leads to renewed fortune.
Bhishma cites an ancient dialogue between Bali and Indra as an illustrative example.
The gods and asuras fought a great war; the daityas and danavas were defeated, Vishnu traversed the three worlds, and Indra became the king of the gods.
The gods received offerings, the four varnas performed their duties, the three worlds prospered, and Ishvara (Shiva) was pleased.
Indra, accompanied by Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, Ashvins, sages, Gandharvas, Nagas, and Siddhas, rode the four-tusked elephant Airavata and toured the three worlds.
One day, Indra saw Bali, son of Virochana, in a seaside cave and approached him.
Bali, seeing Indra surrounded by gods and seated on Airavata, showed no sorrow or distress.
Indra, surprised by Bali's composure, questioned why Bali wasn't grieving despite losing his supreme status, falling into enemy hands, losing strength, sovereignty, wife, and wealth.
Bali responded calmly, chiding Indra for his harsh words and stating that a true hero shows compassion even to a defeated enemy.
